ann_83.original:
Sparse linear backbone plus single-state units, exactly linear on the data: identity_lin = 38 direct input weights (31 state one-hots, voiceMailPlan -0.659, numberVmailMessages +0.453, totalEveCharge +0.515, totalNightMinutes +0.198, totalIntlCharge +0.333, totalDayCalls +0.112, accountLength +0.147) plus 7 relu units on single state one-hots (3741 state:39, 12681 state:44, 16888 state:30, 18605 state:43, 9093 state:31, 7655/27279 state:25) which are affine in their binary input, so each acts as a state offset. Largest offsets are rare-state switches: state:11 (-2.5 logit, 73 rows), state:46 (-2.0), state:4 (+1.4), state:39 (-0.95, mostly via 3741).

Evidence (train, n=4000): Exactly linear (identity node; state units affine on binary inputs, linear R2 1.0). Mean-ablated AUC 0.914 -> 0.890. Setting every state one-hot to 0 everywhere gives AUC 0.906. Per-state logit effect (category on vs off) vs calibrating offset given other features: state:11 -2.49 vs -2.52 (73 rows, 3 churners; raw log-odds offset -1.22), state:46 -1.96 vs -1.96 (80 rows, raw -0.83), state:4 +1.37 vs +1.39 (41, raw +0.84), state:47 +1.20 vs +1.32 (72, raw +0.95), state:39 -0.95 vs -0.95 (82, raw -0.86). The network's state offsets equal the training-calibrated ones, i.e. roughly double the raw offsets: fitted to small samples.
ann_83.proposed: A straight-line part whose main effect is a shift by state.

ann_84.original:
Day x eve bill interaction. 103 = relu(1.554 eveCharge + 0.928) (off below eve charge ~14.5) is read out at -0.717 and passed through the near-identity relu chain 5908 -> 10233 into 9165 = relu(0.609 dayCharge + 0.484*10233 - 0.770*14599 - 0.982), read out at +2.713. Net: at low day charge the cascade cancels the backbone eve-charge slope (down to -2.2 logit), at high day charge it adds up to +2.5 logit when eve charge is also high, i.e. churn rises with the combined day+eve bill. 14599 = relu(0.884 CSC - 0.848) (on from 3 service calls) switches the bill hinge off for complaining customers, so bill and CSC effects do not stack.

Evidence (train, n=4000): Train tables (CSC<=2), cascade logit by day-charge bin (rows) x eve-charge bin (cols, cut at 14.2/17.1/19.9/22.6): day<23: 0.00, -0.30, -0.90, -1.56, -2.16; day 38-42: 0.00, -0.24, -0.16, +0.48, +1.20; day>42: +0.39, +0.42, +1.14, +1.67, +2.48. Observed churn day>42: 0.21, 0.44, 0.65, 0.75, 0.76; day<23: 0.05-0.07 flat (so the cancelled eve slope at low day charge is supported). At top day-charge quintile, cascade mean +0.52 for CSC<=2 vs -0.48 for CSC>=4 (14599 shut-off). 10233 = 1.024*relu(0.941*103 - 0.083 - 0.043 state:3) + 0.005 to within 0.002. Sensitivity: 103/10233 to eveCharge 1.11/1.05, state:5 0.20; 9165 to dayCharge, eve and CSC.
ann_84.proposed: A higher daytime charge raises the predicted chance, more so when the evening charge is high.

ann_85.original:
Customer-service-calls hinge: 11061 = relu(0.441 CSC + 0.058 state:2 - 0.386), read out at +1.965: zero for 0-2 calls, about +0.19 logit at 3 calls, then about +0.66 logit per extra call (+0.85 at 4, +1.53 at 5).

Evidence (train, n=4000): Train: hinge logit by service calls 0..7: 0, 0, 0.01, 0.19, 0.85, 1.53, 2.22, 2.90; observed churn 0.115, 0.110, 0.110, 0.106, 0.437, 0.571, 0.679, 0.545. The jump is between 3 and 4 calls; the +0.19 at 3 calls is slightly early. Linear R2 0.59. Sensitivity: CSC 0.095, state:2 0.012.
ann_85.proposed: Customer-service calls add slightly from about 3 calls upwards.

ann_86.original:
Service calls x low day charge: 13711 = relu(0.754 CSC - 0.609 dayCharge - 0.775), read out at +2.112. It is on only when many service calls coincide with low day charge: about +3.0 logit at 4 calls and day charge < 23, falling to 0 for day charge > 38. Empirically churn at 4 calls is 94% for low-day-charge and 7% for day charge 33-38.

Evidence (train, n=4000): Train table (logit/churn/n) by day-charge bin [0,23.1,28.4,33,38.2,42.4,59.8]: CSC<=2 +0.25/0.06, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0; CSC=3 +1.84/0.08, +0.82/0.04, +0.15, 0, 0, 0; CSC=4 +2.99/0.94/33, +1.94/0.59/44, +1.34/0.39/38, +0.63/0.07/44, +0.05/0.14, 0; CSC>=5 +4.89/1.00, +3.97/0.71, +3.00/0.43, +2.67/0.20, +1.83/0.35, +0.79/0.42. Supported by data at 4+ calls; at 3 calls with day<23 it adds +1.84 though churn is 0.08 (over-extended). Single largest nonlinear gain (restore alone +0.045 AUC). Sensitivity: CSC 0.149, dayCharge 0.119.
ann_86.proposed: For the customers with about three customer-service calls that it acts on, calls add slightly and a higher daytime charge lowers the predicted chance.

ann_87.original:
Near-dead service-call tail: 13489 -> 9657 -> 651 and 8513 -> 5000 (plus small state:11/state:12 weights) are on for only 3 training rows (8-9 service calls), contributing at most +0.64 logit there and 0 elsewhere.

Evidence (train, n=4000): Train: nonzero on 3 rows only (8 or 9 service calls, all churners): +0.24 and +0.64 logit. Logit sd 0.015; removing it changes AUC by <1e-5. Sensitivities ~1e-4.
ann_87.proposed: A part for extreme numbers of customer-service calls that acts on only 3 customers.

ann_88.original:
Heavy-day-usage hinge for customers without voicemail messages: 2149 = relu(0.672 dayCharge + 0.562*relu(0.961 dayCharge - 0.298) - 1.869 numberVmailMessages - 0.020 state:38 - 1.658), read out at +2.038. Zero whenever the customer has any voicemail messages; for vmail=0 it switches on above day charge ~38 and reaches +2.8 logit for the top 10% of day charge (churn 61% there vs 8% with voicemail).

Evidence (train, n=4000): Train table (logit/churn/n) by day-charge bin [0,23.1,28.4,33,38.2,42.4,59.8]: vmail=0: 0/0.15, 0/0.10, 0/0.08, +0.07/0.07, +1.00/0.22, +2.84/0.61; vmail>0: 0 everywhere, churn 0.09,0.08,0.07,0.07,0.04,0.08. The vmail x heavy-day interaction is in the data. Restore alone +0.038 AUC. Sensitivity: numberVmailMessages 0.356, dayCharge 0.234, state:38 0.004.
ann_88.proposed: For customers with no voice-mail messages, a daytime charge above about $36.37 raises the predicted chance.

ann_89.original:
International plan offset: 15558 = relu(0.699 internationalPlan - 0.647) is 0 for plan=no and 1.51 for plan=yes, read out at 1.865: a +2.82 logit offset for international-plan customers (churn 42% vs 11%). Exactly linear in the binary input.

Evidence (train, n=4000): Train: 0 for 3620 non-plan rows, logit +2.82 for 380 plan rows (churn 0.424 vs 0.112). Linear R2 1.0; linearising leaves AUC unchanged; mean-ablated AUC 0.862 (largest single drop). Sensitivity 0.066.
ann_89.proposed: An international plan raises the predicted chance.

ann_90.original:
P(churn) = sigmoid(-1.489 + sum of seven additive children): linear_and_state_offsets (identity_lin, weight 1) + day_eve_cascade (-0.717*103 + 0.082*10233 + 2.713*9165) + csc_hinge (1.965*11061) + csc_lowday (2.112*13711) + csc_tail (2.05*651 + 1.57*5000) + day_novmail_hinge (2.038*2149) + intl_plan (1.865*15558). Composition is purely additive in the logit; the only cross-child coupling is inside day_eve_cascade (service calls switch off the bill hinge). 27 inputs are unconnected (17 state one-hots, all 3 area codes, totalDayMinutes/EveMinutes/NightCharge/IntlMinutes, which duplicate connected charge/minute columns, and eve/night/intl call counts) and have zero effect.

Evidence (train, n=4000): Local train decomposition: full AUC 0.914 (refit L2 logistic regression 0.843). Every child replaced by its least-squares linear fit: 0.839. Restoring one child's nonlinearity onto that: csc_lowday +0.045, day_novmail_hinge +0.038, day_eve_cascade +0.036, csc_hinge +0.017 (all three CSC children together 0.886, +0.047), csc_tail 0, linear/intl 0 (exactly linear). Gains are strongly sub-additive (sum 0.136 vs total 0.075). Linearising one child at a time costs ~0.010 each for cascade, lowday and novmail. Function preservation checked by check_explanation.py.
ann_90.proposed: The predicted chance that a customer leaves rises with an international plan and with a daytime charge above about $36.37, more so with a high evening charge and no voice-mail messages; state shifts it; area code, daytime and evening minutes and several call counts are ignored.

Restoring one child's nonlinearity onto that: csc_lowday +0.045, day_novmail_hinge +0.038, day_eve_cascade +0.036, csc_hinge +0.017 (all three CSC children together 0.886, +0.047), csc_tail 0, linear/intl 0 (exactly linear). Gains are strongly sub-additive (sum 0.136 vs total 0.075). Linearising one child at a time costs ~0.010 each for cascade, lowday and novmail. Function preservation checked by check_explanation.py.

parts.name: linear_and_state_offsets
parts.original_hypothesis:
Sparse linear backbone plus single-state units, exactly linear on the data: identity_lin = 38 direct input weights (31 state one-hots, voiceMailPlan -0.659, numberVmailMessages +0.453, totalEveCharge +0.515, totalNightMinutes +0.198, totalIntlCharge +0.333, totalDayCalls +0.112, accountLength +0.147) plus 7 relu units on single state one-hots (3741 state:39, 12681 state:44, 16888 state:30, 18605 state:43, 9093 state:31, 7655/27279 state:25) which are affine in their binary input, so each acts as a state offset. Largest offsets are rare-state switches: state:11 (-2.5 logit, 73 rows), state:46 (-2.0), state:4 (+1.4), state:39 (-0.95, mostly via 3741).

Evidence (train, n=4000): Exactly linear (identity node; state units affine on binary inputs, linear R2 1.0). Mean-ablated AUC 0.914 -> 0.890. Setting every state one-hot to 0 everywhere gives AUC 0.906. Per-state logit effect (category on vs off) vs calibrating offset given other features: state:11 -2.49 vs -2.52 (73 rows, 3 churners; raw log-odds offset -1.22), state:46 -1.96 vs -1.96 (80 rows, raw -0.83), state:4 +1.37 vs +1.39 (41, raw +0.84), state:47 +1.20 vs +1.32 (72, raw +0.95), state:39 -0.95 vs -0.95 (82, raw -0.86). The network's state offsets equal the training-calibrated ones, i.e. roughly double the raw offsets: fitted to small samples.

parts.name: day_novmail_hinge
parts.original_hypothesis:
Heavy-day-usage hinge for customers without voicemail messages: 2149 = relu(0.672 dayCharge + 0.562*relu(0.961 dayCharge - 0.298) - 1.869 numberVmailMessages - 0.020 state:38 - 1.658), read out at +2.038. Zero whenever the customer has any voicemail messages; for vmail=0 it switches on above day charge ~38 and reaches +2.8 logit for the top 10% of day charge (churn 61% there vs 8% with voicemail).

Evidence (train, n=4000): Train table (logit/churn/n) by day-charge bin [0,23.1,28.4,33,38.2,42.4,59.8]: vmail=0: 0/0.15, 0/0.10, 0/0.08, +0.07/0.07, +1.00/0.22, +2.84/0.61; vmail>0: 0 everywhere, churn 0.09,0.08,0.07,0.07,0.04,0.08. The vmail x heavy-day interaction is in the data. Restore alone +0.038 AUC. Sensitivity: numberVmailMessages 0.356, dayCharge 0.234, state:38 0.004.

parts.name: intl_plan
parts.original_hypothesis:
International plan offset: 15558 = relu(0.699 internationalPlan - 0.647) is 0 for plan=no and 1.51 for plan=yes, read out at 1.865: a +2.82 logit offset for international-plan customers (churn 42% vs 11%). Exactly linear in the binary input.

Evidence (train, n=4000): Train: 0 for 3620 non-plan rows, logit +2.82 for 380 plan rows (churn 0.424 vs 0.112). Linear R2 1.0; linearising leaves AUC unchanged; mean-ablated AUC 0.862 (largest single drop). Sensitivity 0.066.

parts.name: csc_lowday
parts.original_hypothesis:
Service calls x low day charge: 13711 = relu(0.754 CSC - 0.609 dayCharge - 0.775), read out at +2.112. It is on only when many service calls coincide with low day charge: about +3.0 logit at 4 calls and day charge < 23, falling to 0 for day charge > 38. Empirically churn at 4 calls is 94% for low-day-charge and 7% for day charge 33-38.

Evidence (train, n=4000): Train table (logit/churn/n) by day-charge bin [0,23.1,28.4,33,38.2,42.4,59.8]: CSC<=2 +0.25/0.06, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0; CSC=3 +1.84/0.08, +0.82/0.04, +0.15, 0, 0, 0; CSC=4 +2.99/0.94/33, +1.94/0.59/44, +1.34/0.39/38, +0.63/0.07/44, +0.05/0.14, 0; CSC>=5 +4.89/1.00, +3.97/0.71, +3.00/0.43, +2.67/0.20, +1.83/0.35, +0.79/0.42. Supported by data at 4+ calls; at 3 calls with day<23 it adds +1.84 though churn is 0.08 (over-extended). Single largest nonlinear gain (restore alone +0.045 AUC). Sensitivity: CSC 0.149, dayCharge 0.119.
variables: number of calls to customer service

parts.name: day_eve_cascade
parts.original_hypothesis:
Day x eve bill interaction. 103 = relu(1.554 eveCharge + 0.928) (off below eve charge ~14.5) is read out at -0.717 and passed through the near-identity relu chain 5908 -> 10233 into 9165 = relu(0.609 dayCharge + 0.484*10233 - 0.770*14599 - 0.982), read out at +2.713. Net: at low day charge the cascade cancels the backbone eve-charge slope (down to -2.2 logit), at high day charge it adds up to +2.5 logit when eve charge is also high, i.e. churn rises with the combined day+eve bill. 14599 = relu(0.884 CSC - 0.848) (on from 3 service calls) switches the bill hinge off for complaining customers, so bill and CSC effects do not stack.

Evidence (train, n=4000): Train tables (CSC<=2), cascade logit by day-charge bin (rows) x eve-charge bin (cols, cut at 14.2/17.1/19.9/22.6): day<23: 0.00, -0.30, -0.90, -1.56, -2.16; day 38-42: 0.00, -0.24, -0.16, +0.48, +1.20; day>42: +0.39, +0.42, +1.14, +1.67, +2.48. Observed churn day>42: 0.21, 0.44, 0.65, 0.75, 0.76; day<23: 0.05-0.07 flat (so the cancelled eve slope at low day charge is supported). At top day-charge quintile, cascade mean +0.52 for CSC<=2 vs -0.48 for CSC>=4 (14599 shut-off). 10233 = 1.024*relu(0.941*103 - 0.083 - 0.043 state:3) + 0.005 to within 0.002. Sensitivity: 103/10233 to eveCharge 1.11/1.05, state:5 0.20; 9165 to dayCharge, eve and CSC.
variables: number of calls to customer service

parts.name: csc_hinge
parts.original_hypothesis:
Customer-service-calls hinge: 11061 = relu(0.441 CSC + 0.058 state:2 - 0.386), read out at +1.965: zero for 0-2 calls, about +0.19 logit at 3 calls, then about +0.66 logit per extra call (+0.85 at 4, +1.53 at 5).

Evidence (train, n=4000): Train: hinge logit by service calls 0..7: 0, 0, 0.01, 0.19, 0.85, 1.53, 2.22, 2.90; observed churn 0.115, 0.110, 0.110, 0.106, 0.437, 0.571, 0.679, 0.545. The jump is between 3 and 4 calls; the +0.19 at 3 calls is slightly early. Linear R2 0.59. Sensitivity: CSC 0.095, state:2 0.012.

parts.name: csc_tail
parts.original_hypothesis:
Near-dead service-call tail: 13489 -> 9657 -> 651 and 8513 -> 5000 (plus small state:11/state:12 weights) are on for only 3 training rows (8-9 service calls), contributing at most +0.64 logit there and 0 elsewhere.

Evidence (train, n=4000): Train: nonzero on 3 rows only (8 or 9 service calls, all churners): +0.24 and +0.64 logit. Logit sd 0.015; removing it changes AUC by <1e-5. Sensitivities ~1e-4.

reference_patient.definition: the typical patient: the median training patient for every number and the most common training category for every category (not a real patient)

confidence_rules.clearly: a meaningful change in predicted risk for a typical patient (at least 5% points), the test split agrees (same sign, and its bootstrap interval over test patients excludes no benefit), and every group has at least 20 training patients
confidence_rules.consistently across patients: the claim holds for at least 90% of training patients (range across patients); this is not a significance statement
confidence_rules.on the training data only: the test split disagrees (opposite sign, or no benefit on test patients) or is unclear (its interval includes no benefit), or no test check is available
confidence_rules.slightly: the change in predicted risk for a typical patient is below 5% points
confidence_rules.the model has little data on this: a compared group has fewer than 20 training patients

settings.effect_scale: log-odds (output pre-activation) for verification; predicted risk for the typical patient for wording
